feature: The pick on top, the lists in a pane at the bottom
summary: The right panel now splits like Photoshop's Properties over Layers: what you picked scrolls on top, and Layers, Measurements and Library share a pane at the bottom that keeps its height whatever you pick. A line between them drags to share the height.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default (next-lists-pane is on at Next). Walks: panel-shows-what-is-picked-walk, panel-shows-what-is-picked-video-walk.

try.do: New blank canvas with the Library shown, nothing picked. The top part is empty and the pane at the bottom holds Layers and Library.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Draw a rectangle (U), press V. Appearance, Effects and Motion lead the panel; Layers sits in the pane below.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the line above Layers up. The pane grows until its lists fit, and stays that tall after you pick something else.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press I for Measure with nothing picked. Measure Tool sits alone on top, the pane is unchanged.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Draw a distance, press V and click its row in Layers. The caliper's own sections fill the top; the Layers row you clicked does not move.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Open a recording and pick the clip. On a video the panel stays one column: the clip's sections, then Captions and Transitions.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Does picking a row in Layers now feel steady, with the list staying where your pointer is?
Is the pane's starting height (40 per cent, or enough for Layers and the Library's first row) right on your usual window?
With nothing picked, is an empty top part fine, or would you rather see something there?
Is the line between the two parts easy enough to find and grab?
rough: On a video, Captions and Transitions stay at the foot of the pick's column rather than in the pane: in the pane they pushed a picked sound's Fades below the fold on a laptop window. That is the card on-a-video-captions-and-transitions-sit-where-th-do-captions-and-transitions-join, task on-a-video-captions-and-transitions-sit-where-th.

The shared mock shell stacks Layers above Properties in one dock (UX-PATTERNS shell item 6); the panel now puts the pick on top with the lists in a pane, as you chose on the card the-right-panel-shows-only-what-the-picked-thing-where-do-layers-and-library-sit (your call on 2026-10-13).

Section counts in the pick's part, before (one column, Layers included) to after (top part only, pane apart): nothing picked 2 to 0, rectangle 5 to 3, rectangle with Measure 6 to 4, nothing with Measure 3 to 1, caliper 7 to 4, text 7 to 4, screenshot 2 to 0. The video states are unchanged (clip 10, title 8).
The line between the parts is a plain hairline with a resize cursor, like a Mac split view; there is no visible grabber.
On a short window the pane can be shorter than Layers and the Library at their least, and then it scrolls on its own.
